title: Guided Fleet Route Across a City Grid
real_world_story: A delivery vehicle moving across a city grid wants to reach a delivery destination while exploring as few blocks as possible. Some blocks are blocked and cannot be crossed. A guided search uses a heuristic that estimates the remaining distance to the destination so that it explores promising directions first.

real_world_connection.input_represents: A grid of city blocks with blocked and open cells
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Guided pathfinding that searches fewer cells toward the destination

problem_statement: Given a grid of R rows and C columns where 0 represents an open cell and 1 represents a blocked cell, a start cell and a target cell, find the length of the shortest path from the start to the target moving only through open cells up, down, left or right. The algorithm may use a heuristic to guide the search.
task: Find the minimum number of steps from the vehicle to the delivery destination, or -1 if it is unreachable.
input_format: The first line contains two integers R and C. The next R lines each contain C integers (0 or 1). The next line contains four integers SR, SC, TR, TC representing the 0-based start and target coordinates.
output_format: Print the minimum number of steps from the start to the target, or -1 if the target is not reachable.
constraints: Multiple paths may exist; the answer is the shortest.

expected_algorithm.name: A* Pathfinding
expected_algorithm.reason: On a grid with a known destination, a Manhattan-distance heuristic guides the search toward the target and often explores fewer cells than an unguided search.

hint: Estimate the remaining distance with a heuristic such as Manhattan distance.
Always expand the cell with the smallest sum of cost so far and heuristic.
Stop as soon as the destination cell is expanded.
real_world_takeaway: Guided pathfinding such as A* lets delivery vehicles reach their destinations efficiently, reducing time in dense city grids.
